messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed a regression in per-token TTFT after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. p50 TTFT for short prompts jumped ~30ms, but decode time stayed ~same. wondering if kernel attribution is wrong or batching heuristics interacting with KV cache. see summary below.

kevin: ugh. can you paste the profiling snapshot?

maria: pasted quick numbers: p50_total_ttft=72ms -> 104ms (after), p50_decode=40ms -> 42ms. kernel_exec_time reported +28ms. KV cache hit-rate unchanged (~87%). :thinking:

maria: also saw more frequent small batches during peak but batch size distribution looks same on aggregate. curious if a new kernel path increases per-call overhead (kernel init / descriptor).

perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression-detected service=runtime component=kernel-selector delta_p50=32ms link=https://perf.local/alerts/3456 :rotating_light:

sophie: can you run the instrumented trace with kernel_time attribution? I added a split metric last week: runtime_token_ttft{stage="ttft"}, runtime_token_ttft{stage="decode"}, runtime_token_ttft{stage="kernel"}.

raj: fwiw the kernel selector rollout only flipped the "prefer-optimized-kernel" flag for models with seq_len<=128. maybe the optimized kernel has higher setup costs.

maria: here is the prometheus query I used to generate the breakdown:
```
# p50 TTFT stages over 5m
quantile_over_time(0.5, runtime_token_latency_seconds{stage=~"ttft|decode|kernel"}[5m])
```

eli: try this to get per-route attribution for short chat vs long-form:
```
# p50 kernel time for route /v1/generate where seq<=128
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(runtime_kernel_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",seq_bucket="<=128"}[5m])) by (le,route))
```

maria: ran a flamegraph on a few samples — kernel stack shows a new path: kernel_loader:init_descriptors -> cudnn_conv_prepare -> kernel_dispatch_smallseq. that descriptor alloc adds ~20-30ms in many traces.

kevin: descriptor alloc smells like repeated per-call allocations. we should persist descriptors per worker if possible. did we disable descriptor caching with the new selector?

sophie: good catch. the selector toggles a "use_dynamic_desc" flag to enable fewer kernels precompiled. it's possible we regressed on small seq by enabling dynamic descriptors that allocate at runtime.

raj: suggest experiment: roll back flag on 1 canary node and compare TTFT distribution (p50/p95) + kernel_time. also test with batching disabled for a short window to see if per-call alloc compound with frequent small batches.

maria: starting canary roll-back now on canary-3. will monitor.

perf-bot: [deploy] rollback started canary=canary-3 user=maria ts=1755001423

kevin: also add a metric runtime_descriptor_allocs_total{kernel_variant} so we can graph alloc rate per kernel.

eli: i pushed a tiny patch to the tracer to emit trace/span attribute kernel.variant and descriptor_alloc (bool). query will be easier after that.

sophie: for dashboards, we should surface a per-route split: TTFT={network+queue+kernel+decode} with kernel further broken by variant. i'll sketch a panel and share.

maria: rollback looks promising so far — p50_total back to 75ms after 3m, kernel_time p50 down ~22ms. keeping monitor.

raj: if rollback confirms, plan: revert flag, add descriptor caching and add unit test for descriptor reuse under high small-batch rates. file an RFC for kernel-selector logic to include descriptor-cost heuristics.

maria: filing RFC now: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/rt-kerne-desc-cost (draft).

kevin: can we also add synthetic load test that simulates bursty small requests (seq<=64) — to catch regressions earlier?

eli: yeah I'll add a workload to perf-suite: small-chat-bursts. will link results.

perf-bot: [note] regression resolved on canary-3. monitoring continues.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: kevin -> descriptor caching PR; eli -> perf-suite workload; sophie -> dashboard panel; raj -> RFC + tests. i'll update thread when PRs land. :thumbsup:
